issues.body:
The note explains the revision as a single counting bug: the old pair counter 'dropped PRs whose changed-file list was empty, conflating a failed read with a genuinely empty PR', and the corrected run 'keeps genuinely empty PRs as non-colliding participants, excludes and names only failed reads'.

Follow that through. The corrected participant set = (PRs with a non-empty file list, unchanged) + (genuinely empty PRs) - (failed reads, still excluded). Genuinely empty PRs share no file with anyone, so they add zero to the numerator; failed reads are excluded, so they add zero. The count of pairs sharing >=1 changed file therefore MUST be unchanged at 6 (ci) and 2 (docs). Only the denominator can grow.

The table instead reports 40 and 30. Under the described methodology on the same data that is impossible, and it moves the rates in the wrong direction: the described fix alone would yield 6/435 = 1.4% and 2/630 = 0.3%, i.e. a STRONGER case for the exemption, not the weaker 9.2%/4.8% presented.

The likeliest real explanation is that this is a NEW, larger snapshot (ci holders 16 -> 30, docs 12 -> 36) rather than a re-run over the old one. That is a legitimate thing to do, but it is not what the note says, and it silently invalidates the next paragraph's 'Measured counterfactual on that same snapshot' - whose frontier 1/2/3/4 numbers were measured on the retracted snapshot and are not re-derived here.

For a block explicitly labelled HONESTY NOTE, the explanation must account for its own numbers.
issues.fix_hint: State what actually changed. If the corrected run is over a new snapshot, say so and date it, e.g. 'remeasured on a fresh 2026-09-01 snapshot (30 ci holders, 36 docs holders); the earlier table's 16/12 holder counts reflect the 2026-07-28 snapshot'. Separate the two effects: how much of the delta is the empty/failed-read fix versus snapshot growth. If the failed reads were previously being silently dropped WITH their real file lists (which would explain a numerator rise), reword - that is a different bug from 'dropped genuinely empty PRs'. Also either re-measure the counterfactual (baseline frontier 1; ci 2; ci+docs 3; deps 4) on the new snapshot or change 'that same snapshot' to name the older one explicitly, and record the failed-read count the note promises to 'name'.
issues.title: Honesty note's stated cause cannot account for the 6->40 / 2->30 rise in colliding pairs

issues.body:
scripts/tests/test_readiness_visibility.py::test_the_declaration_records_its_measured_basis reads this file, slices the basis block (head[head.rindex('# ------'):] before 'NON_RESERVING_PARTITIONS = ') and asserts the tokens 'area:ci', 'area:docs', 'area:deps', 'Cargo.lock', '5%', '3%', '100%', '57.1%', 'crate-region-parallelism.md' all appear. Its docstring states the purpose: 'the next reader must be able to RE-DERIVE the decision rather than guess at it. Asserted on the numbers, not on prose.'

I ran that assertion logic against the PR head. It passes - but only because '5%' and '3%' survive inside the new sentence that declares them RETRACTED. The test now pins figures the file says are wrong, and does not pin 9.2%/4.8% at all. I confirmed it is vacuous by mutating the source: 9.2% -> 99.9% and 4.8% -> 88.8% leaves the test GREEN.

This is the surviving-mutant class the test class itself says the estate keeps measuring, and it is exactly the guard that should have caught an unreviewed edit to the measured basis.

Related stale prose in the same test file (not in this diff, but falsified by it): the TestNonReservingCrossCuttingPartitions docstring at ~line 1636 still asserts as current fact 'The justification is a MEASURED conflict rate, not an argument (see NON_RESERVING_PARTITIONS for the table): 5% of open area:ci holder pairs and 3% of area:docs pairs share a changed file'. Per this PR that sentence is now false.
issues.fix_hint: Update the token list in test_the_declaration_records_its_measured_basis to pin the authoritative figures - replace '5%', '3%' with '9.2%', '4.8%' - so a future edit to the table goes red. If the retraction line should also be pinned, assert it separately and distinguishably (e.g. assert 'retracted' appears near '120/6'), so presence of the old tokens can never be what makes the test green. Also fix the class docstring at ~line 1636 to quote 9.2%/4.8%, since this PR falsifies it.
issues.title: Pinning test still asserts the retracted 5%/3% and passes only via the retraction sentence; new figures unpinned

issues.body:
Two paragraphs below the corrected table, the block still reads: '`ci`/`docs` reservation never serialised PR-vs-PR contention at all (14 open PRs co-hold `ci` and 10 co-hold `docs` right now, concurrently ...)'.

The new table implies 30 ci holders (435 = C(30,2)) and 36 docs holders (630 = C(36,2)). So the co-hold sentence is inconsistent with the table it is supporting, and it also reverses the ordering: the table now has docs holders > ci holders (36 > 30) while the sentence has ci > docs (14 > 10). The old table (16 ci / 12 docs) was at least directionally consistent with it; the new one is not.

A reader re-deriving the decision from this block gets two different populations for the same partitions, in the same comment, with no indication which snapshot each belongs to. Since the sole purpose of this PR is to make these figures trustworthy, leaving a contradicting count in place undercuts it.
issues.fix_hint: Re-derive the co-hold counts from the same run that produced 435/630 and update them to match (or label them with their own snapshot date if they are deliberately from the earlier measurement). Ideally state the holder counts explicitly in the table itself - e.g. 'area:ci  30 holders  435 pairs  40 sharing (9.2%)' - so the nCr denominators are checkable by inspection and there is one authoritative population per partition.
issues.title: Unrevised holder counts later in the same block now contradict the new table

issues.body: The percentage column lost its alignment: the ci/docs rows use '(9.2%)   ->' and '(4.8%)   ->' (three spaces) while the retained deps/crate rows use '(100%)  ->' and '(57.1%) ->'. The counts column shifted too ('435         40' vs '  3          3'). The block is a hand-aligned ASCII table, so the drift is visible.
issues.fix_hint: Re-pad the four data rows so the holder-pairs, sharing, percentage and '-> exempt' columns line up as they did before.
issues.title: Table columns no longer align after the figure update

verdict.summary:
Comment-only change to the measured basis for NON_RESERVING_PARTITIONS in scripts/ready-issues.py. No executable code changes; the frozenset({'ci','docs'}) declaration and every predicate (partition_path, keys_conflict, non_reserving_partitions, reserves_partition) are untouched, so there is no behavioural, soundness, or security risk, and the exemption decision itself still holds at the corrected rates (9.2%/4.8% remain far below deps 100% and crate 57.1%).

The arithmetic is internally consistent and I verified it: 435 = C(30,2), 630 = C(36,2), 40/435 = 9.20%, 30/630 = 4.76% -> 4.8%, matching the stated 'each denominator is nCr'. The retracted figures also check out (120 = C(16,2), 6/120 = 5%; 66 = C(12,2), 2/66 = 3.03%).

But this PR's entire content is a claim about measurement provenance, and three things do not hold up.

(1) The stated cause cannot produce the stated numbers. The correction described only ADDS genuinely-empty PRs as 'non-colliding participants' and still EXCLUDES failed reads. Neither group can contribute a colliding pair, so the numerator must be unchanged at 6 and 2. It instead rose to 40 and 30. On the same snapshot that is self-contradictory; if the snapshot changed, that is undisclosed and breaks the 'that same snapshot' reference two lines below.

(2) The pinning test was not updated. scripts/tests/test_readiness_visibility.py::test_the_declaration_records_its_measured_basis asserts the literal tokens '5%' and '3%' are present in this block. I ran its assertion logic against the PR head: it passes, but only incidentally, because those strings survive inside the retraction sentence itself. The new authoritative figures are unpinned - I mutated 9.2%->99.9% and 4.8%->88.8% and the test stayed GREEN. Coverage of the measured basis is now vacuous.

(3) Stale figures in the same comment block now contradict the new table (see issues).

Requesting changes on (1) and (2); otherwise low-risk and directionally an improvement in honesty.
